title: Preflight ops mini-townhall talks
content:
Context / purpose:
- Short (10-12 minute) mini-townhall for ops+platform; audience ~30 (SRE, infra, oncall leads + a handful of eng managers).
- Goal: align on new weekend preflight checklist, temporary tweaks to handback window, and reassure product teams about minimal user-facing risk.
- Tone: pragmatic, transparent, focused on what we’re changing and why. No engineering deep-dive.

Opening (30s):
- Quick hello, name, role, why ops handoffs mattered last quarter (one sentence).
- 'This is a short sync to make a small set of changes less scary — not an alarm.'

Why now (90s):
- Two recent late-night handbacks where the KV cache invalidation + autoscaler race caused degraded latency for a subset of routes. Root cause: competing autoscaler policies + a stale prefix cache flush.
- Customer impact was limited (few timeouts, retries) but operational toil spiked.
- We have a short-term mitigations bundle and a mid-term config hardening plan.

What we’re changing (3–4 bullets, 3 min):
- Preflight checklist: mandatory for any weekend maintenance window. Critical items: autoscaler policy lock, cache drain window, fallback routing validation. (Link to checklist in Confluence.)
- Handback window change: extend from 30m -> 45m for weekends for routes with >5k RPS or expensive KV prefix states. Rationale: observed 20–30m tail events; buffer reduces risk.
- Canary cadence tweak: smaller canary batches (5% -> 2%) for model/serving changes during weekend windows.
- Fast fallback: we’ll keep the current fallback model pool but enable a guarded auto-promote path for the last 15m of the handback window.

Operational playbook highlights (1.5 min):
- Owner: oncall lead who opens the window. Required: tagging the window in PagerDuty + Slack channel #ops-handbacks.
- Checklist must be signed off by two people OR one person + automation tool 'preflight-check'.
- If any step fails, immediate rollback AND escalate to SRE triage rotation.

Suggested comms script for oncall (30s):
- 'We’re starting the weekend handback window for namespace X. Preflight checks green. Rolling traffic validations in progress. If you see 5xx or 90th p99 > 2s, ping #ops-handbacks and call the triage channel.'

FAQ / Q&A crib (notes for the presenter) (3 min):
Q: Will this increase weekend latency?
A: No. The extended handback window is a harmless buffer for operators; it is not an extra maintenance window. Production traffic routing should be unchanged unless a rollback or fallback is triggered.

Q: How does this affect Dedicated customers?
A: Dedicated pools are unaffected unless they opt into the shared handback tooling. We’ll notify active Dedicated customers 48 hours in advance if we plan any cross-pool changes (that's a separate cadence).

Q: Are we changing SLAs?
A: No SLA changes. This is an ops control to reduce the probability of user-visible incidents.

Q: Who signs the checklist?
A: Oncall lead + one peer (could be the release engineer, or automated signoff via preflight-check CI job).

Scripted answers for sensitive prompts (quick copy):
- If asked about 'why we didn’t prevent this earlier': 'We had heuristics tuned for steady state; recent traffic patterns during holiday surge revealed an edge case for cache invalidation combined with autoscaler churn. The checklist and config guard address that specific gap.'
- If asked about 'backlog of infra work': 'We prioritized highest customer-impact work first; this is now in the critical path and has a scheduled fix in the next two sprints.'

Follow-ups & homework (for meeting ends) (bullet list):
- Ops: finalize the preflight-check automation in infra repo (PR #512) — @Rowan. Target: Wed 03/18.
- SRE: publish short runbook (one pager) for handback failures — @Marta. Target: Fri 03/14.
- PM/Product: send a heads-up to top 5 customers in the next 48 hours (templated note in Confluence). Owner: @Liya (ask product comms).
- Engineering leads: review and sign off on canary size change for your services by EOD Thursday.

Open questions / notes to self (scratchy):
- Consider adding an automated telemetry check (k/v cache hit ratio + 95th token latency) to the preflight tool. Feels doable but needs infra cycles.
- Need to confirm Dedicated pool opt-in UX (is it an environment flag or a kickoff form?). Follow up with Private deployments team.
- Check legal/comms for customer announcement wording (we want 'informational' not 'apology').

End script (20s):
- Reiterate: short change, low customer impact, higher operator confidence. Ask for a quick thumbs-up from leads in the thread.

Post-meeting (notes):
- Share recording + Confluence link in #ops-handbacks and pin.
- Create small retro template to capture any flaps during next weekend window (automated form).

Draft email blurb to product owners (two-sentence):
- 'Heads-up: starting this weekend we’re enforcing a small preflight checklist and slightly longer weekend handback buffer for routes with high KV state. We don’t expect user-visible changes; this is to reduce regression risk and lower night-shift incident mobilization. Contact ops if you rely on time-sensitive deployments.'

Stylistic/performer notes:
- Keep language plain, avoid blame. Say 'we observed' not 'you/they did'.
- Use one concrete example (non-prod replica) to explain the timing issue if asked.
- Don't read verbatim; use bullets as prompts.

---
Scratch TODOs before presenting:
- @Rowan: confirm PR link and automation demo (due 3/12).
- @Marta: upload runbook draft to Confluence (due 3/14).
- @Sasha: rehearse 2x with Rowan, pull 1-2 screenshots of telemetry.
- Add the short FAQ to the townhall slide footer.

(End of scratch notes)
